The strongest refutation is "It is impossible to calculate all the consequences of one's acts." The calculus requires summing the pleasures and pains of every consequence of an act, including far-reaching and unforeseeable ones. If those consequences can't be known and totalled, the calculus can't be used. The other option, "Pain and pleasure are inevitable features of life," is no objection at all, because it doesn't touch the calculus's method.

CONFIDENCE: 82
